question_text: In the 0/1 Knapsack problem with weights `W` and items `N`, why must the 1D space-optimized DP array `dp[w]` be traversed backwards from capacity `C` down to item weight `w_i`?

options.text: To allow SIMD vectorization on modern CPUs
To prevent using the current item multiple times in the same transition
To avoid array index out of bound exceptions
To guarantee that smaller weights are computed first

answer_explanation: Traversing backwards guarantees that `dp[w - w_i]` represents the optimal value from the *previous* item iteration (item `i-1`). A forward traversal would use values already updated with item `i`, inadvertently modeling the unbounded knapsack problem.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: B. Rationale: Traversing backwards guarantees that `dp[w - w_i]` represents the optimal value from the *previous* item iteration (item `i-1`). A forward traversal would use values already updated with item `i`, inadvertently modeling the unbounded knapsack problem.
